identification.summary: Storm-3127 is a Microsoft Threat Intelligence designation for a financially motivated actor; Microsoft's naming mapping lists UNC6240 (Mandiant / Google TI) as the corresponding vendor name [S1]. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) describes UNC6240 as the cluster that conducts extortion of victims whose Salesforce data was stolen by the separate cluster UNC6040, consistently claiming to be 'ShinyHunters' [S2]. No Microsoft publication describing Storm-3127 directly was located in open search, so the profile below rests on GTIG reporting about UNC6240 and assumes the Microsoft-to-Mandiant mapping in [S1].
identification.notes: UNC6240 is distinct from UNC6040 (vishing / initial access and data theft) in GTIG's naming; GTIG suspects a possible partnership [S2]. 'ShinyHunters' is a claimed identity, not confirmed attribution [S2]. Do not merge facts about UNC6395 (Salesloft Drift / Gainsight OAuth token theft, which Google says overlaps with ShinyHunters activity) into this cluster without a source that makes the link [S5]. Microsoft's exact cluster boundary for Storm-3127 is not publicly documented in sources found.

attribution.sponsor: Non-state, financially motivated (no state sponsor stated in sources) [S1][S2]
attribution.confidence: Microsoft classifies the actor as financially motivated [S1]; GTIG describes UNC6240 as financially motivated extortion activity and notes the ShinyHunters name is only a claimed affiliation [S2]. Individual-level attribution is not established in the cited GTIG report.
attribution.basis: Microsoft naming-mapping entry equating Storm-3127 with UNC6240 [S1]; GTIG observation that UNC6240 extortion messages consistently claim ShinyHunters, and sender addresses shinycorp@tuta[.]com and shinygroup@tuta[.]com [S2]. Separate press reporting describes French arrests in June 2025 of people using the ShinyHunters handle in connection with BreachForums [S6]; no source found ties those individuals to UNC6240 specifically.

objectives: Monetary gain through extortion of organizations whose cloud (Salesforce) data was stolen; demands were bitcoin payment within 72 hours [S2].

sectors: Multinational corporations (sectors not enumerated in the GTIG report) [S2]
Technology (Google disclosed one of its own corporate Salesforce instances was accessed) [S2]
regions: English-speaking users at multinational corporations; no specific countries named by GTIG [S2]
targeting.notes: Victim selection follows the UNC6040 data-theft intrusions, with extortion surfacing in some cases months afterward [S2]. Extortion contacts were made by calls and emails to employees of victim organizations [S2].

capabilities.summary: UNC6240 capability observed by GTIG is extortion tradecraft: phone and email pressure on victim employees, bitcoin payment demands with a 72-hour deadline, use of the ShinyHunters brand to raise pressure, and possible preparation of a data leak site [S2]. The upstream data theft attributed to UNC6040 used voice phishing of IT-support pretext to have users authorize a modified Salesforce Data Loader connected app (some named 'My Ticket Portal'), later custom Python scripts, with Mullvad VPN and TOR anonymization and lateral movement to Okta and Microsoft 365 [S2]. Whether the same operators perform both phases is unconfirmed [S2].

campaigns.name: Salesforce vishing data theft followed by ShinyHunters-branded extortion
campaigns.summary: GTIG reported UNC6040 vishing campaigns against Salesforce instances and noted that extortion by UNC6240, claiming to be ShinyHunters, occurred months after intrusions, suggesting a possible partnership [S2].

campaigns.name: Google corporate Salesforce instance accessed
campaigns.summary: GTIG updated its report to disclose that one of Google's own Salesforce instances holding SMB contact information was accessed in June 2025; data was limited to basic, largely public business information [S2].

campaigns.name: Gainsight-linked Salesforce data theft attributed by Google to ShinyHunters-overlapping activity
campaigns.summary: Press reporting says Google was aware of more than 200 potentially affected Salesforce instances after the Gainsight incident and that ShinyHunters activity overlaps with what Google tracks as UNC6395; this is a different Google cluster from UNC6240 and linkage to Storm-3127 is unverified [S5].

campaigns.name: French arrests of suspected ShinyHunters-handle users
campaigns.summary: Press reporting says French police reportedly arrested four BreachForums-linked individuals in late June 2025 (SiliconANGLE counts five arrests including IntelBroker, arrested earlier in February), with the ShinyHunters handle among those reported; relationship to UNC6240 is not established in sources [S6].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated extortion actor claiming the ShinyHunters identity; Microsoft Storm-3127 equated with GTIG UNC6240 [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Extortion by phone and email with bitcoin demands; related UNC6040 vishing and Data Loader abuse supplies the stolen data [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Tuta email addresses shinycorp@tuta[.]com and shinygroup@tuta[.]com used for extortion; related intrusion activity used Mullvad VPN and TOR [S2].
diamond.victim: Employees and organizations whose Salesforce data was stolen, mainly English-speaking users at multinationals [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal monetization; GTIG notes overlaps with actors in 'The Com' communities and says similarities may reflect shared communities rather than coordination [S2].
diamond.technology: Salesforce (connected apps, Data Loader), Okta and Microsoft 365 as pivot targets, bitcoin for payment, anonymization services [S2].

gaps: No Microsoft primary publication on Storm-3127 found; the Storm-3127 to UNC6240 equivalence rests only on Microsoft's naming mapping file [S1].
Relationship between UNC6240, UNC6040, UNC6395 and the broader ShinyHunters / Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters collective is not fully resolved in cited sources [S2][S5].
Whether a data leak site was launched, and its infrastructure, was not verified in sources opened.
Pages for TechCrunch, Infosecurity Magazine, CyberInsider and the Huntress ShinyHunters profile appeared in search results but could not be opened; S5 and S6 rely on search-result summaries.
Later 2026 activity (Okta SSO vishing under other UNC clusters, arrests reported 2026) was seen only in secondary summaries and is not tied to Storm-3127 [S7].
Government indictments or advisories were not reviewed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: relevant cyber terrain is cloud SaaS tenants (Salesforce) with connected apps, plus identity providers (Okta) and Microsoft 365 reached by lateral movement [S2]. Step 3: adversary is a criminal extortion actor, not state-sponsored per cited sources [S1][S2]. Step 4 MLCOA: social-engineering of help desk or end users to authorize a malicious connected app, bulk data export, then threatening calls and emails to employees with 72-hour bitcoin deadlines [S2]. MDCOA: escalation via a leak site and wider pivot into identity and email platforms [S2]. Candidate indicators: unexpected connected-app authorizations, large Data Loader or API exports, Mullvad/TOR source IPs, extortion mail from the listed Tuta addresses [S2]. Direct relevance to military networks is not established by sources; applicability to DoD or contractor SaaS tenants is an inference.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track GTIG and Microsoft reporting on this cluster and on naming overlaps [S1][S2]. Authorities: response to a criminal extortion actor against contractor or mission-partner SaaS would normally fall to defensive and law enforcement channels rather than offensive authorities; confirm with legal. Mission assurance: restrict API Enabled, Manage Connected Apps and Customize Application permissions, allowlist connected apps, enforce IP restrictions and universal MFA, and monitor large downloads, as GTIG recommends [S2]; train help-desk and personnel on vishing [S2]. Coordination: share indicators with cloud and identity providers and mission partners; employees should report extortion calls promptly [S2].
